title: The Impossible Garden
premise: Ivo Ishikawa has spent ten years writing letters to a stranger he met once, in a hospital waiting room, and never saw again — letters he never sent, kept in a drawer beneath the register of his bookshop. When Wren Alcott moves into the cottage next door to recover from a career-ending injury as an investigative journalist, Ivo recognizes the handwriting on the return address of a letter he finally mailed last spring. Wren came to the town chasing a corruption story that implicates the family who own half its businesses — including the development threatening Ivo's shop and his daughter's school. As their decade-long correspondence becomes a real, fragile love, Wren's investigation makes them both targets, forcing Ivo to choose between the safety of silence and speaking, at last, the sentence he rehearsed for ten years. In the end, they publish the truth together, save the shop by turning it into the town's free lending library, and Ivo says the sentence — not as a confession of the past, but as a promise about the future.
about_author: Casper Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent years watching strangers fall in love over recommended novels. They write romances about people who are braver on paper than in person.

chapters.title: The Drawer Beneath the Register
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Morning routine at Ishikawa Books: opening the till, making cocoa for his daughter Noor, and touching the drawer where 120 unsent letters sleep. A developer's notice on the door threatens demolition. Emotional beat: tenderness armored by routine; we learn love lives in past tense for him.

chapters.title: The Moving Truck
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A moving truck idles outside the long-empty cottage next door; through the rain Ivo glimpses a stranger wrestling a bookshelf alone. He carries out tea without being asked. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity cracking his solitude open one inch.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Alcott unpacks a life reduced to boxes: a shattered shoulder ended their journalism career, or so everyone believes. They recognize the town from a postcard they once received — unsigned. Emotional beat: exile disguised as retreat; a secret purpose humming under the quiet.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren visits the bookshop; Ivo recommends a novel whose margins contain notes in handwriting Wren knows intimately — their own old hand, from letters written a decade ago. Neither says anything. Emotional beat: recognition withheld, hearts pounding behind polite conversation.

chapters.title: Noor's Map
chapters.summary: Noor's POV (age nine). Noor, sharp and lonely since her mother left, sketches a map of the town marking 'safe places' and 'scary places,' and quietly adds the new neighbor to the safe column. Emotional beat: a child's clear-eyed hope doing what her father cannot.

chapters.title: The Letter That Got Away
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback woven into present: the hospital waiting room ten years ago, the stranger who shared his umbrella and one honest hour, and the single letter Ivo finally mailed last spring after the demolition notice arrived. Emotional beat: grief reframed as unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Story Wren Is Chasing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At night Wren works: the Halloway family's development company has been buying the town with poisoned loans, including the note on Ivo's shop. Wren didn't come here to heal; they came to finish the story that destroyed their career. Emotional beat: duty sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Cocoa and Confessions
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Noor drags Ivo to the cottage; Wren feeds them stew, and Ivo almost mentions the letters but swerves. Wren notices the swerve. Emotional beat: two people fluent in evasion, reading each other anyway.

chapters.title: What the Margins Said
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns to the shop and buys the annotated novel, comparing marginalia to their kept copies of Ivo's decade of letters — because Wren wrote back, every year, to a P.O. box, and never got an answer. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing you've been loved longer than you knew.

chapters.title: The Eviction Vote
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Town council, chaired by Marcus Halloway, fast-tracks the demolition. Ivo speaks publicly for the first time in years and fails; Wren watches him break slightly and decides the story is no longer abstract. Emotional beat: public humiliation forging private resolve.

chapters.title: Rain, Again
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Caught in a storm sheltering under the same awning geometry as ten years ago, Ivo and Wren share an umbrella and a kiss that neither planned. Emotional beat: the past tense collapsing; terror and joy arriving together.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. That night Ivo opens the drawer and reads the first letter aloud to himself — the sentence he has rehearsed for a decade: not 'I love you' but 'I should have said.' He cannot yet say it to Wren's face. Emotional beat: courage measured in inches.

chapters.title: Halloway Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Marcus Halloway offers Wren money to walk away, revealing he knows exactly why they're here — and hints he knows about the letters too. Wren refuses. Emotional beat: threat made personal; the stakes turn from story to survival.

chapters.title: Broken Trust
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo discovers Wren's investigation files while returning a borrowed coat — and realizes Wren may have approached him as a source, not a neighbor. He leaves without a word. Emotional beat: the oldest wound reopened by the newest hand.

chapters.title: Noor Runs
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Hurt by the cold war between the adults she loves, Noor runs to the cottage in the rain; Wren finds her feverish and calls Ivo. The three spend a terrible, tender night together. Emotional beat: crisis dissolving pride; family assembling itself by accident.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren shows Ivo everything: the ledger evidence, the threats, and the shoebox of replies they wrote yearly to the dead P.O. box. Ivo shows the drawer. One hundred twenty letters meet their answers. Emotional beat: a decade of misdelivered love finally delivered.

chapters.title: Going Public
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren plans to publish despite the legal risk; Ivo insists the shop be the distribution point — a hundred printed copies handed across his counter. Noor designs the cover. Emotional beat: fear converted into choreography; justice as a community act.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Halloway's men vandalize the shop; Ivo and Wren repair it until dawn, gluing spines, laughing shakily. Ivo nearly says the sentence and stops — 'not like this, not out of fear.' Emotional beat: intimacy deepened by shared damage; restraint as devotion.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The story breaks: the town reads it in the bookshop doorway, the council collapses, a state investigation opens. Halloway confronts them and is recorded by half the town. Emotional beat: triumph that feels strangely quiet — the real climax is still owed.

chapters.title: The Question of Staying
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. With the story done, Wren's old paper offers their job back in another city. Wren prepares to leave rather than presume; Ivo, terrified of asking, lets them pack. Emotional beat: love against duty inverted — each sacrificing for the other wrongly.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the bus stop, Noor hands Wren a letter — the 121st, which she stole from the drawer weeks ago. Ivo finally says it aloud: 'I should have said this ten years ago: stay. Not because I need saving. Because I choose you.' Wren misses the bus on purpose. Emotional beat: the decade-long rehearsal ending in a single spoken line.

chapters.title: The Impossible Garden
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. Spring: the shop reopens as a free lending library, Wren writes from the desk by the window, and in the lot behind the store — where demolition was cancelled — Noor plants a garden everyone called impossible. Emotional beat: love kept in present tense at last.
